meta.title: Future Tenses Test - Gen Z Themes
meta.description: A comprehensive test covering English Simple Future Tenses
meta.info: This test includes 30 questions focusing on combined grammar structures involving Future Simple, Future Continuous, Future Perfect, and Future Perfect Continuous, paired with topics like conditionals, passive voice, gerunds, and more, all within familiar Gen Z contexts.
meta.author: Qwen3.7

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: If the TikTok algorithm _____ my video, it _____ viral by tomorrow morning.

explanation.text: This combines the First Conditional with the Future Simple tense. The 'if' clause uses the present simple ('pushes'), and the main clause uses 'will' + base verb ('will go') to predict a future result.
explanation.concept: Predicting future outcomes based on present conditions
explanation.formula: If + subject + present simple, subject + will + base verb
examples: If it rains, we will cancel the picnic.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with a time clause. 'Will have been playing' is required to show duration up to a future point, and 'for' is used with a period of time, not 'since'.
explanation.concept: Expressing duration up to a specific future moment
explanation.formula: By the time + present simple, subject + will have been + verb-ing + for + time
examples: By the time you arrive, I will have been waiting for an hour.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: By 2030, single-use plastics _____ in many countries to protect the oceans.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with the Passive Voice. The action will be completed before a future time ('By 2030'), and the subject receives the action.
explanation.concept: Completed future actions in the passive voice
explanation.formula: By + future time, subject + will have been + past participle
examples: By next year, the bridge will have been completed.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with a non-defining relative clause. 'Will have been training' is required to emphasize the duration of an action up to a future point.
explanation.concept: Duration up to a future point within a relative clause structure
explanation.formula: By + future time, noun, who + has/have + past participle, will have been + verb-ing
examples: By June, the band, which has toured extensively, will have been performing for a decade.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: I am considering _____ my screen time, so I _____ to delete some distracting apps.

explanation.text: This combines the 'be going to' future form with a gerund verb pattern. 'Consider' is followed by a gerund ('reducing'), and 'am going' expresses a planned future intention.
explanation.concept: Planned future actions and verbs followed by gerunds
explanation.formula: Consider + verb-ing; Subject + am/is/are + going + to-infinitive
examples: I am thinking about moving, so I am going to save money.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Simple tense with modal verbs and comparatives. 'Will' cannot be directly followed by 'can'; 'will be able to' is the correct future form of 'can'. Also, 'more happier' is a double comparative error; 'happier' is sufficient.
explanation.concept: Future ability and correct comparative forms
explanation.formula: Subject + will be able to + base verb; Subject + will make + object + comparative adjective
examples: Students will be able to learn online, which will make them more independent.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: While you _____ your favorite true crime podcast, I _____ a guided meditation session.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with a present continuous time clause. 'While' + present continuous sets the background action, and 'will be leading' describes another action in progress at that same future time.
explanation.concept: Parallel actions in progress at a specific future time
explanation.formula: While + subject + present continuous, subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: While you are studying, I will be cooking dinner.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with a time clause and verb patterns. The time clause requires the present simple ('launches'). 'Promise' is followed by a to-infinitive, so 'to have fixed' is the correct perfect infinitive form.
explanation.topic: Future Perfect + Time Clauses + Verb Patterns
explanation.concept: Present simple in future time clauses and perfect infinitives
explanation.formula: By the time + subject + present simple, subject + promise + to have + past participle
examples: By the time he arrives, we promise to have finished the work.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: Thrifting _____ more popular than fast fashion as Gen Z _____ more eco-conscious.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Simple tense with a comparative structure and an 'as' clause indicating a simultaneous future trend. The main clause uses 'will become', and the subordinate clause uses the present simple 'becomes' to state a general future truth.
explanation.concept: Predicting future trends and comparisons
explanation.formula: Subject + will + base verb + comparative + as + subject + present simple
examples: Electric cars will become cheaper as technology improves.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with prepositions of time. 'Will have been' is required to show duration up to a future point ('By midnight'), and 'for' is used with a period of time, not 'since'.
explanation.concept: Duration up to a future point and correct time prepositions
explanation.formula: By + future time, subject + will have been + verb-ing + for + period of time
examples: By 5 PM, I will have been working for eight hours.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: The university _____ a new mental health center next semester, which _____ a huge difference for students.

C.text: will have opened / will have made

explanation.text: This combines the Future Simple tense with a non-defining relative clause. 'Will open' predicts a future event, and 'will make' predicts the future result of that event.
explanation.concept: Predicting future events and their consequences
explanation.formula: Subject + will + base verb + , which + will + base verb
examples: The company will launch a new product, which will change the market.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with the Passive Voice. The stage receives the action, so the future passive 'will be decorated' is required, not the active 'will be decorating'.
explanation.concept: Future actions in the passive voice
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + past participle + by/with + agent
examples: The house will be painted next week.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the time the food delivery arrives, I _____ starving, so I might regret _____ so much.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Simple tense with a gerund verb pattern. 'Will be' describes a future state, and 'regret' is followed by a gerund ('ordering') when referring to a past action that one feels sorry about.
explanation.concept: Future states and verbs followed by gerunds
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + adjective; regret + verb-ing
examples: I will be tired, so I might regret staying up late.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Simple tense with quantifiers. 'A few' is used with countable plural nouns ('plants'), and 'isn't much' is used with uncountable nouns ('light').
explanation.concept: Correct quantifier usage with countable and uncountable nouns
explanation.formula: Subject + will + base verb + a few + countable noun; there + isn't much + uncountable noun
examples: I will buy a few books because there isn't much space.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: If I adopt a rescue dog, I _____ taking it to the park every morning.

explanation.text: This combines the First Conditional with the Future Continuous tense. The 'if' clause uses the present simple, and the main clause uses 'will be' + verb-ing to describe a habitual future action.
explanation.concept: Predicting habitual future actions based on a condition
explanation.formula: If + subject + present simple, subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: If I get the job, I will be working from home.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with a time clause. In future time clauses introduced by 'once', 'when', or 'by the time', we use the present simple ('starts'), not the future simple ('will start').
explanation.concept: Present simple in future time clauses
explanation.formula: Once/When/By the time + subject + present simple, subject + will have + past participle
examples: When she arrives, we will have finished dinner.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the end of the month, I _____ my workout streak for 30 days, so I _____ a reward.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with the Future Simple tense. 'Will have maintained' shows an action completed before a future time, and 'will claim' predicts the subsequent future action.
explanation.concept: Completed future actions leading to subsequent future actions
explanation.formula: By + future time, subject + will have + past participle, so + subject + will + base verb
examples: By Friday, I will have finished the report, so I will take a break.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Passive voice with subject-verb agreement. 'Episodes' is plural and receives the action, requiring 'will be released'. 'Host' is singular, requiring 'is going to'.
explanation.concept: Future passive constructions and singular/plural agreement
explanation.formula: Plural subject + will be + past participle; Singular subject + is + going to + base verb
examples: The letters will be sent tomorrow, and the manager is going to call.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: This time next summer, we _____ across the country, _____ in national parks.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with a present participle clause. 'Will be driving' describes an action in progress at a specific future time, and 'staying' provides additional simultaneous information.
explanation.concept: Actions in progress at a specific future time with additional context
explanation.formula: This time + future, subject + will be + verb-ing, + verb-ing + prepositional phrase
examples: This time tomorrow, I will be flying, reading a book.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Simple tense with modal verbs and conditionals. Two modal verbs ('must' and 'will') cannot be used together. 'Will' is the correct choice for a First Conditional prediction.
explanation.concept: Correct modal usage in future conditional sentences
explanation.formula: Subject + will + base verb + if + subject + present simple
examples: We will succeed if we try hard.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: To ace the exam, I _____ all night, so I _____ to drink a lot of coffee.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with the 'be going to' future form. 'Will be studying' emphasizes the duration of the future action, and 'am going' expresses a planned intention.
explanation.concept: Emphasizing future duration and planned intentions
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + verb-ing, so + subject + am/is/are + going + to-infinitive
examples: I will be working late, so I am going to order dinner.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with gerund verb patterns. 'Will be' must be followed by a present participle ('making'). 'Avoid' is always followed by a gerund ('being').
explanation.concept: Future actions in progress and verbs followed by gerunds
explanation.formula: Subject + will be + verb-ing; avoid + verb-ing
examples: I will be sleeping, so I will avoid being woken up.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the time the photography exhibition opens, all the photos _____ by a professional.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with the Passive Voice. The action will be completed before a specific future time ('By the time... opens'), and the subject receives the action.
explanation.concept: Completed future actions in the passive voice
explanation.formula: By the time + present simple, subject + will have been + past participle
examples: By tomorrow, the house will have been cleaned.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the 'be going to' future form with a relative clause. 'That' or 'which' must be used for objects ('sneakers'), not 'who'. After 'will', the base form of the verb ('cost') is required.
explanation.concept: Relative pronouns for objects and base verbs after modals
explanation.formula: Noun (object) + that/which + subject + am/is/are + going to + base verb, will + base verb
examples: The book that I am going to read will take hours.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: By the end of this project, I _____ on it for six months, so I _____ a long vacation.

B.text: will have been working / will take

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect Continuous tense with the Future Simple tense. 'Will have been working' emphasizes the duration of an action up to a future point, leading to a future decision ('will take').
explanation.concept: Duration up to a future point leading to a future action
explanation.formula: By + future time, subject + will have been + verb-ing, so + subject + will + base verb
examples: By December, I will have been saving for a year, so I will buy a car.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Simple tense with quantifiers. 'Some' is used with uncountable nouns ('water'), and 'much' is used with uncountable nouns in negative sentences ('thirst').
explanation.concept: Correct quantifier usage with uncountable nouns
explanation.formula: Subject + will + base verb + some + uncountable noun; don't have much + uncountable noun
examples: I will buy some bread because I don't have much time.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: While you _____ the next episode, I _____ the snacks.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Continuous tense with a present continuous time clause. 'While' + present continuous sets the background action, and 'will be preparing' describes another action in progress simultaneously.
explanation.concept: Parallel actions in progress at a specific future time
explanation.formula: While + subject + present continuous, subject + will be + verb-ing
examples: While you are sleeping, I will be cleaning.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with verb patterns. 'Expect' is followed by a to-infinitive ('to release'). The Future Perfect requires 'have' + past participle ('changed').
explanation.concept: Verbs followed by to-infinitives and past participles in perfect tenses
explanation.formula: Subject + expects + to + base verb + that + will have + past participle
examples: He expects to finish the project that will have improved sales.

data.hint: Choose the correct verb forms to complete the sentence.
data.question: I _____ my old clothes to a thrift store tomorrow, because I enjoy _____ them a second life.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Simple tense with a gerund verb pattern. 'Will donate' expresses a future decision or promise, and 'enjoy' is always followed by a gerund ('giving').
explanation.concept: Future decisions and verbs followed by gerunds
explanation.formula: Subject + will + base verb; enjoy + verb-ing
examples: I will visit my grandma because I enjoy spending time with her.

data.hint: Click the incorrect parts and type the correct form.

explanation.text: This combines the Future Perfect tense with the Passive Voice. The correct structure is 'will have been' + past participle, not 'will have being'.
explanation.concept: Correct formation of the future perfect passive
explanation.formula: By + future time, subject + will have been + past participle + by + agent
examples: By tomorrow, the work will have been completed by the team.
